sentences.text:
Shri Suhas Pundlik - Government Advocate for respondent
Record of the Court below has been recived.
Appeal is admitted for final hearing.
Also heard on I.A. No.3788 of 2023, which is an application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail and suspension of remaining jail sentence on behalf of appellant Kedar Nagar.

Appellant has been convicted under Section 420 of IPC and Section 6 (1) of M.P. Nikshepakao Ke Hito Ka Sanrakshan Adhiniyam, 2000 and has been sentenced to undergo 5 years R.I. with fine of Rs.2,000/- and 5 years R.I. with fine of Rs.50,000/- respectively with usual default stipulation.

entities.text: M.P. Nikshepakao Ke Hito Ka Sanrakshan Adhiniyam, 2000
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submit that appellants is an innocent person and he has been falsely implicated in this matter.

Appellant has already suffered jail incarceration for more than 4 years and 6 months, which is about 90% of the total awarded jail sentence and final conclusion of this appeal would take sufficient long time.
There is a strong case in favour of the appellant.

Hence,
the execution of the remaining part of the jail sentence of the appellant be suspended till the final disposal of this appeal.
Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / State opposes the application for suspension of sentence and prays for its rejection.

Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, nature of the allegation levelled against the appellant and also taking note of the fact that appellant has already suffered 90% of total awarded jail sentence and final conclusion of the appeal will also take sufficient long time.
In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, I find it is to be a fit case to suspend the remaining custodial sentence of the appellant.
